A_OUTERMOST_BOUNDARY.design: The pre-node boundary gained an OUTER layer built from trusted OS primitives (db/custody/pre-node-boundary.ts PRE_NODE_OUTER_BOUNDARY_CMD): C:\Windows\System32\cmd.exe /d /c <channel-dir>\d1-pre-node-outer-boundary.cmd <plan>. cmd.exe is native (not a CLR process), /d disables AutoRun; the .cmd clears PSModulePath and every CLR-profiler / startup-hook input (COR_*, CORECLR_* incl. _32/_64, DOTNET_STARTUP_HOOKS, DOTNET_ADDITIONAL_DEPS) in a localized scope, then launches Windows PowerShell and the launcher by ABSOLUTE paths (SystemRoot for powershell.exe, %~dp0 for the script), never through PATH resolution.
A_OUTERMOST_BOUNDARY.inner: The inner PowerShell script was rewritten to make every trust decision with .NET APIs and language primitives (System.Environment.GetEnvironmentVariables, System.IO.File, System.Security.Cryptography.SHA256, System.Diagnostics.Process), never an autoloadable cmdlet a poisoned PSModulePath could shadow; it reads the environment with a .NET API before anything could autoload, refuses every Node/OpenSSL/loader input and every CLR-profiler / startup-hook input present at entry, and clears PSModulePath. ConvertFrom-Json is module-qualified.
A_OUTERMOST_BOUNDARY.not_claimed: A check inside an already-compromised PowerShell process is not sufficient and is not claimed to be; PSModulePath is neutralized by the .NET-only path plus the outer clear, not by refusing its mere presence (PowerShell always populates it).
A_OUTERMOST_BOUNDARY.measured: tests/custody/d1-pre-node-boundary.test.ts (27/27 on this Windows host; the cross-platform subset also under pwsh on Linux CI). CONTROL: the malicious PSModulePath module is armed — imported it executes and runs the node trojan. Through the boundary (direct inner AND end-to-end through the outer cmd): 0 malicious module executions, 0 trojan node executions, 0 secret prompts; the channel still runs (probe OBSERVED). The inner refuses COR_PROFILER / CORECLR_PROFILER / DOTNET_STARTUP_HOOKS present at entry. The outer cmd (Windows) clears those inputs and removes the attacker PSModulePath entry before PowerShell. The R4 NODE_OPTIONS preload attack still refuses with 0 preload executions.

B_UTC_CANONICALIZATION.design: IP-4 closed with one canonical UTC parser (utcMillis in d1-mint-operator-evidence.ts): regex for the two canonical shapes, Date.UTC, finite check, and an exact re-serialization round-trip. Date.parse is never used. Impossible-but-plausible timestamps normalize to a different instant and are rejected.
B_UTC_CANONICALIZATION.measured: tests/custody/d1-oep1-evidence-chain.test.ts: month 13, day 00, day 31 of September, Feb 29 of a common year, hour 24, minute 60, leap second :60, missing Z, an offset instead of Z, a one-digit fraction, a non-date and a non-string are all rejected; a leap-year Feb 29 is accepted; a SINGLE-record chain with an impossible timestamp does not close, and a two-record chain cannot order itself by an impossible predecessor time. The chain rule and PMR-14 are unchanged; only the time predicate is stricter.

C_CASE_STABLE_DISCOVERY.design: Governed OEP-1 evidence identity is the tracked Git path, not the working-tree filename casing (discoverOep1RecordNames). Inside a git work tree, discovery enumerates git ls-files (exact tracked case); reading the tracked name returns the content on any filesystem casing; a case divergence between tracked and on-disk, an untracked governed file, or a tracked file missing from the working tree is an integrity failure. Outside a git work tree the working-tree listing is used and the history check reports it unverifiable.
C_CASE_STABLE_DISCOVERY.measured: A case-only rename (_v -> _V) is reported as an integrity failure and never silently removes the FAIL from the chain while git is clean (the tracked lower-case name stays in the discovered set); an untracked governed evidence file is refused; a fully tracked, matching working tree raises no reason. Tested on Windows semantics here and cross-platform on CI.

D_PMR16_HOSTNAME.design: PMR-16 behaviorally proves hostname verification (hostnameVerificationReasons in d1-tls-trust-harness.ts, used by trustTextBehaviourReasons / measureServerAuthentication): the built checkServerIdentity is invoked with a certificate whose names match the host (must accept) and one whose names do not (must reject).
D_PMR16_HOSTNAME.measured: tests/custody/d1-dag-amendment-v1010.test.ts: a function that always accepts the peer hostname, one that always rejects, and a missing function each make PMR-16 fail; Node's real checkServerIdentity passes; the CONFORMING trust text passes the behavioral gate on the repository CA. The certified trust text is byte-identical to b4ca05ac (only the measurement was strengthened).
